comment: L2B feedback-governance thresholds. Every number here was calibrated against a recorded failure in EVENTS.md; changing one changes what wakes L2B.

looping.comment: H-DEAD-25: bg_19 re-launched calibrate_v2.py four times while the real defect was one unguarded divide. Three relaunches with no gate between is the point where relaunching stopped being exploration. A gate run, pass or fail, resets both runs: verification is the loop breaker. The stream is the telemetry writer's session-events.jsonl - the live transcript, including the files a compaction boundary rolled past, which is where a loop's evidence used to vanish. gate_patterns is the writer's gate vocabulary; max_event_age_s drops a stream left behind by a session that already stopped, so a dead session cannot manufacture a loop finding.

interpreter_noise.comment: verbosity/warning flags whose value is not the target; -c and -m carry the program, so their payload is the identity

progress_stall.comment: calibrated 2026-11-19 on the omp transcript corpus (manifest_sha256 75463ff2c7f2952188c8d2742627879919d506679b43ab5e5c2588002045de6c, 253 transcripts, 1299984656 bytes, 1661 labelled repeat increments): a gate-free stretch of >= 60 events whose events-per-distinct-target ratio reaches 3 fires on 5 churn intervals (rate 0.0338) and 7 intervals that ended in a passing gate (rate 0.0015). The grid's looser settings (N12/R2) reach 0.0163 on normal work, which is where a wake stops being a signal. ORDER_MIN holds at share_bound_first 0.9375, so when a per-identity bound crosses inside the same stretch the bound lane owns it and this lane keeps silent.

referent.comment: A SHA is only a referent break when the grammar around it claims commit identity: a bare hash beside sha256/digest/receipt is an artifact digest and lives on disk, not in git. run/ is gitignored box-local liveness evidence, so a cited run/ path whose basename exists somewhere is recorded as path drift (a note, not a surprise); only a basename absent from the whole repo means the artifact was never written here.

post_compact.comment: H-DEAD-11/19: after a boundary the model re-emits an edit/write block from evicted memory and the payload corrupts the call. H-DEAD-32: a node stamped pass whose gate script has since moved is a pass for code that no longer exists, so the node's gate command AND the scripts its evidence names are both staleness referents. turn_file points at the telemetry writer's elided slice (tool-call arguments and result payloads removed), so a hit is a marker the model itself emitted in text, not the harness's own block skeleton.

test_regression.comment: H-DEAD-31: a gate run as `... | head -20` returns head's exit status, so a failing suite is recorded as a pass; `| tail -N` without pipefail does the same to the suite's own exit code. A red or unstamped gate_result is a pass claim with no time coordinate, which is unfalsifiable.

response.comment: 120 tokens with gamma_down = 1.0: the block must be readable in one glance and cost less than the next wasted launcher. Token counts come from the live tokenizer when reachable (max_tokens=1, usage.prompt_tokens); the divisor is the estimate used when it is not, and it is deliberately conservative.

l2b.comment: The loop lane reads an event stream it does not produce. This is the step that keeps that stream current: an audit asks the writer for a fresh slice of the transcript belonging to telemetry_cwd (default: the auditing process's own cwd) before scanning. A writer that is missing, times out or finds no transcript costs a gap note, never a false pass and never the audit itself.

comment_top: Two layers, one boundary. L2A (spine_check/plan_check via the hook and the commit boundary) is feedforward: it fires where a discontinuity is already known. L2B (this policy) is feedback: it sleeps through normal execution and wakes only on an anomaly. default_repos lists what L2B GUARDS; ref_repos lists what it may RESOLVE a citation against - guarding every repo on the box would make the DORMANT claim unprovable.
